title: Tech News 2026 – Issue 44
content:
Latest tech news from the Wikimedia technical community. Please tell other users about these changes. Not all changes will affect you. Translations are available.

Weekly highlight

  • An experiment launched on September 29 is testing article recommendations for new account holders who also identify as readers. By suggesting articles to read, similar to recommendations in the Wikipedia app for logged-in readers, the experiment aims to encourage new account holders to read and return to the website regularly, with the goal of increasing internal referrals by 1%. See the related Community Wishlist proposal.
  • Several Wikimedia services were taken offline last week because of a security vulnerability in PHP. This is because they need to be updated before they are safe to put back online. This is not a problem just for the Wikimedia movement but affects a lot of websites. You can follow updates on Wikitech. Cloud VPS and Toolforge will take longer to bring back online. This is to make sure that applications which run on Cloud VPS or Toolforge are not affected. Tool developers can see updates and more information on the Cloud-announce mailing list. [1][2]

title: What Happens After the Merge
content:
A year in the Wikimedia technical community, and why a merged patch is where a contribution starts, not where it ends.

My first patch to Wikimedia software needed a lot of work. I did not really understand code review or why the automated checks had failed, and I submitted it half expecting nobody to reply. Someone did. They explained what was wrong and what I could try next, instead of simply closing it.

That reply is one of the reasons I am still here. It is also why I believe a merged patch is where a contribution starts, not where it ends.

For most of my life, I knew Wikipedia mainly as a reader. I did not realise that software, tools, and a large open-source community sat behind it, or that I could contribute to any of them. An introduction to the Wikimedia ecosystem and the Road to Wiki programme changed that.

I began learning about MediaWiki, the software behind Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects; Gerrit, where code changes are reviewed; and Phabricator, where tasks are tracked. I set up my development environment, submitted patches, worked through review comments, and tried again.
snippet: A year in the Wikimedia technical community, and why a merged patch is where a contribution starts, not where it ends.
creator: Kavaljeet Singh

title: A little bit of everything: My Wikimedia CEE Meeting 2026 Cluj-Napoca notes
content:
This year’s Wikimedia CEE Meeting took place at Babeș-Bolyai University in Cluj-Napoca, Romania. In this post, I have compiled the key moments from CEEM 2026 that stood out to me.

First of all, Cluj-Napoca is a very nice and equally lively city. The open-air concerts and movie screenings we happened to come across while walking around the city in the evenings gave me a sense of its vibrancy.

At this year’s Learning Day, I attended the “Photo Workshop: Practical Photography & Commons Workflows” session because of my interest in photography. During the session, after Gheorghe taught us technical details such as photographic styles, contrast, and light, we put what we learned into practice by taking photos in the garden.

The most important takeaway from this session is that we can experiment with light as much as we want, and these experiments can yield very high-quality daily and artistic photos. It all depends on how we use the light source.

title: Mabia Holds First Quarter Team Meeting to Review Progress, and Upcoming Projects
content:
The Mabia team held its First Quarter Team Meeting on October 18, 2026, via Zoom, bringing members together to review recent developments, discuss micro-grant applications, and plan upcoming Wikimedia activities across the Mabia language communities.

The meeting opened with remarks from Sadik, who thanked everyone who contributed to the successful organization of the Language Diversity Conference held in Accra from October 2 to 4, 2026. He also announced the approval of Wali Wikipedia, congratulating the team on this important development for the Wali language community. He further updated members on the Mabia Individual and Community Micro Grants, noting that the Kusaal and Gurene communities were applying for the micro grants, while the Wali and Dagaare communities had received rapid grants.

title: Verify Before You Contribute: Connecting Fact-Checking with Wikipedia Editing
content:
I participated in the Abuja edition of the Interactive Media Seminar for Electoral Integrity, organised by the Foundation for Investigative Journalism and Accountability (FIAP) through FactCheckAfrica, in collaboration with Wikimedia Nigeria. The seminar was held from 28 to 30 September 2026 as part of the European Union’s support to the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) in the areas of peace, security, and governance.

The seminar brought together Wikimedia contributors, newsroom editors, and fact-checkers for practical sessions on information disorder, source verification, digital investigations, and the responsible creation, contribution, and use of information.

The experience provided an opportunity to learn new skills, reinforce existing knowledge, and reflect on practical ways to identify and counter misinformation. One of the most important lessons I learned was the need to investigate and verify information before believing it, sharing it, or using it to contribute to online knowledge platforms.

title: Learning, Sharing, and Connecting: My First Experience at Open Knowledge in the CEE Region
content:
Sometimes, a conference is valuable not because it answers your questions, but because it helps you discover which questions to ask next.

That was my experience at Open Knowledge: Wikimedia & Research in the CEE Region in Katowice, Poland. I arrived hoping to share my experience of using Wikipedia in university teaching and to meet researchers working on similar topics. But I was also a newcomer, still learning about the wider Wikimedia movement and the community behind the projects I had brought into my classroom.

I had designed and taught my first Wikipedia-based course at Abdullah Gül University in Kayseri, Türkiye, and I wanted to share what my students and I had learned. I also hoped to discover new tools, meet people with similar interests, and explore opportunities for future collaboration.
snippet: Sometimes, a conference is valuable not because it answers your questions, but because it helps you discover which questions to ask next.
creator: Leplebi

title: Wikimedia Foundation Senior Manager Veronica Thamaini Visits Dagbani Wikimedians User Group in Tamale
content:
On October 8–9, 2026, the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group (DWUG) had the pleasure of hosting Veronica Thamaini, Senior Manager of Regional Funding Programs at the Wikimedia Foundation, at its office in Tamale, Ghana. The two-day visit provided an opportunity to showcase our work across the Mabia language communities, reflect on our achievements, discuss ongoing challenges, and explore opportunities to strengthen and sustain our impact.

The visit combined cultural exploration with strategic discussions on language preservation, free knowledge, education, community development, and the future of Wikimedia projects in Ghana.

On October 8, we visited Red Clay Studio and the Savannah Centre for Contemporary Art (SCCA) in Tamale to explore the region’s vibrant creative and cultural landscape, learn more about initiatives preserving and promoting artistic expression, and share some of the cultural spaces that make northern Ghana unique.

The visits also underscored the importance of documenting and making cultural knowledge accessible, values that closely align with our commitment to preserving and sharing knowledge through Wikimedia projects.

title: Wikimedia Jakarta Community’s Bonding Night Trip: Exploring Knowledge and Building Togetherness in the Land of the Kanekes Baduy Luar
content:
The community event of bonding night, known as Makrab (Malam Keakraban), returned as part of GSF26, with the Wikimedia Jakarta Community warmly and enthusiastically welcoming the occasion.

Coordinated by Kume Gucci and Hzu Hzu, who served as treasurer, the event brought together 13 participants for a community bonding night trip in Kanekes, home to the Baduy people.

The event took place on September 5–6, 2026, in the Kanekes area, Leuwidamar District, Lebak Regency, Banten Province. This year’s Wikimedia Jakarta Community bonding trip focused on Kanekes, Lebak, Banten, which is known as the home of the Baduy people.

The location was chosen because of its relatively close proximity to Jakarta and its potential to offer insights into local culture and ways of life that could be documented and shared through Wikimedia projects, particularly Wikimedia Commons and Wikivoyage.

title: From an idea to a content partnership: discover the Content Partnerships Hub
content:
Do you have an idea for a content partnership but need help taking the next step? Are you working with a cultural institution, an educational organisation or a public agency and looking for advice, contacts or technical expertise?

The Content Partnerships Hub Helpdesk helps Wikimedians to find support for collaborations that bring knowledge and freely reusable content to Wikimedia projects: whether you are exploring your first partnership or navigating a challenge in an established project, the Helpdesk offers a place to ask questions and connect with relevant experience across the movement.

The Hub involves many different kinds of work. Some projects might require advice on releasing material under an open licence, preparing a collection for Wikimedia Commons, working with structured data, or finding someone with experience in a particular institution or subject. And that expertise does exist across the Wikimedia movement, but finding the right person or resource can take time and resources. And this is where the Helpdesk helps make those connections.

We offer support that includes:

  • Developing a partnership idea: identifying practical next steps and the support a project may need.

title: Murals for free culture: Schools in Córdoba celebrate Wikipedia’s 25th anniversary
content:
Painting the mural at the Gobernador López school (Córdoba, Argentina)

The “25×25 Celebrando Wikipedia” project took place between February and September 2026 in Córdoba, Argentina, where we commemorated and celebrated Wikipedia’s 25th anniversary through the collective creation of two Wikipedia-inspired murals, while promoting Wikimedia projects, open access, and Creative Commons licenses. Implemented in one primary school and one secondary school in partnership with the Colectivo Artístico ALLI -Arte Libre Laboratorio e Innovación, the project involved students in learning activities about Wikipedia and in artistic production, which culminated in the painting of the murals together with families and community organizations.

The process, documented and shared on Wikimedia Commons, included workshops on Wikimedia projects, particularly Wikipedia, as well as on free culture and Creative Commons licenses.

Students designed images based on what they had learned, representing the philosophy of Wikipedia, Wikimedia Commons, and free culture. They then decided which images would go on the mural, as well as the colors to be used.
snippet: Painting the mural at the Gobernador López school (Córdoba, Argentina)
creator: Monarufino

title: At Wikimedistas de Bolivia, we work with our academic idol, and this is what happened
content:
These days, writing is complex. Writing well is even more so. Through various activities and workshops, we discovered that the community of editors in Bolivia was eager to take their Wikipedia edits a step further.

If we think of it as a craft—because our work is a craft—our writing will always be something that can be refined and improved. Virginia Ayllón at the workshop for Wikipedians

As passionate editors, we often joke that having an article deleted or receiving a warning from a librarian for not following certain conventions is part of an editor’s résumé—let’s say a small bump in the road on the path to becoming a Wikipedian on the Spanish Wikipedia. Even though we try to take it in stride, we know that collaboratively creating content involves many challenges, a lot of practice, and also making mistakes and enjoying the learning process.

title: From Access to Participation: Reflections from OASPA 2026
content:
Following my talk last year at the 4th Open Conference on Open Scholarship in Japan, I was thrilled to be invited to the OASPA 2026 Conference in Zagreb, Croatia, as an opening keynote speaker. The conference took place from 21 to 23 September and brought together members of the global open access community to exchange perspectives, share experiences and explore new approaches to advancing open access. The programme brought together researchers, publishers, librarians and open knowledge practitioners through keynote presentations, panel discussions, interactive sessions and opportunities for networking and exchange.

The opening keynote panel focused on the question “How does open knowledge contribute to society?”, bringing together perspectives from different areas of the open knowledge ecosystem. I joined Nataliia Sokolovska and Nokuthula (Noks) Mchunu for the discussion, moderated by Ben Johnson.

title: Beyond the Workshop: How the Electoral Integrity Seminar Opened New Doors for My Wikimedia and Media Work
content:
From 28 to 30 September 2026, I participated in the Interactive Media Seminar for Electoral Integrity at Reiz Continental Hotel in Abuja, Nigeria. The three-day programme brought together Wikimedia contributors, journalists, media executives, fact-checkers and other professionals working to promote accurate information and address misinformation and disinformation.The seminar was organised by ECOWAS and FIAP, in collaboration with FactCheckAfrica and Wikimedia User Group Nigeria, with co-funding from the European Union and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark. It focused on the role of verified information in strengthening electoral integrity, promoting peaceful elections and improving public access to reliable knowledge ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections.

As a Wikimedia contributor, media professional and community organiser, I joined the programme with an interest in strengthening my fact-checking skills and understanding how Wikimedia projects could contribute to a more reliable information environment. title: Reading Wikipedia in the Classroom: Three Workshops to Promote Digital Literacy and Critical Thinking Among Al Madina School Students in Casablanca
content:
As part of the Reading Wikipedia in the Classroom project, three educational workshops were organized on October 6, 7, and 8, 2026, for students at Al Madina School in Casablanca, in partnership between Wikimedia Morocco User Group and Al Madina School.

The workshops were coordinated and facilitated by Loubna Ait Oumasste, Education Project Coordinator, and Hayat Ahlamine.

This initiative aimed to strengthen students’ digital literacy and develop their critical thinking skills when engaging with online information. It also introduced Wikipedia as one of the world’s leading free knowledge projects and an open educational resource that can be effectively integrated into teaching and learning.

The workshops provided an opportunity for students to explore Wikipedia, understand its fundamental principles, and discover the importance of free knowledge and the role of volunteers in making information accessible to everyone.

  • Introducing Wikipedia and Wikimedia projects.
  • Understanding how encyclopedic content is collaboratively created and improved.
  • Distinguishing between reliable information and information that requires further verification.

title: More Than One Language: How WikiTour Supports Indigenous Language Documentation
content:
Indigenous languages are valuable treasures for every community because they carry its knowledge, history, and identity. However, not all languages have the same opportunities to be documented and made visible to a wider audience online. In addition, online language documentation is especially important in this digital age. Wikimedia projects offer people from all walks of life opportunities to document their languages while making knowledge related to their cultures more accessible to everyone.

WikiTour is one initiative that supports the preservation and documentation of Indigenous languages. In Malaysia, this initiative was started by Kelab Wiki Kent, and throughout 2024 and 2025, the programme involved three Indigenous languages: Kadazandusun, Iban, and Semai. At the same time, it demonstrates how a single initiative can create opportunities for multiple Indigenous languages to be documented.

WikiTour began in 2024 and continued with WikiTour 2.0 in 2025. Throughout these editions, participants were introduced to Wikimedia projects, particularly Wiktionary, where they contributed language knowledge, especially vocabulary.
